summary: Contestants use advanced desktop publishing skills to create creative marketing materials. All work is completed on-site using provided computers and software, and entries are uploaded electronically. Any secondary or postsecondary student may enter.
time_limits: no more than ten (10) minutes orientation
no more than ninety (90) minutes testing time
no more than ten (10) minutes wrap-up
submission_requirements: All student-produced jobs completed on-site are uploaded electronically and are not printed at the national level
what_to_bring: Published and/or unpublished non-electronic written reference materials
Optional - Mac computer. Contestant must also bring software and extension cords. Carry-in and setup of equipment must be done solely by the contestant within the time allotted
competencies: Apply advanced and modern graphic design principles & elements—including layout, color theory, typography, and visual hierarchy—to create cohesive, visually compelling designs for print and digital media
Develop advanced creative concepts and original artwork that visually communicate themes, messages, and brand identity to clients and stakeholders
Utilize advanced technical skills and industry-standard software to edit, manipulate, and optimize graphics, artwork, and images for diverse design applications
judging_notes: AI Policy Level 1 No AI Allowed
No equipment, supplies or materials other than those specified for an event are allowed in the testing area
Previous Business Professionals of America tests and/or sample tests (handwritten, photocopied or keyed) may not be taken into the testing area. Violation of this rule will result in disqualification
Contestants can use software templates, but creativity points may be reduced
At NLC, contestants will take the Desktop Publishing II (YouScience) certification with their contest. Reference materials are not allowed for certification testing
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this application event
